Alex W: Quick plan — run a small exact-conditions smoke to repro the p95 regression we saw yesterday. Goal: apples-to-apples decode with identical prompts, tokenizer, and decoding params; compare kernel selection + batching effects + KV warmup.

Alex W: Command I ran last night (example):
```
./replay_harness --trace=2026-03-15T22Z \
  --model=redwood/gptx-8q \
  --kernels=auto \
  --decode='temp=0.0,top_p=0.92,seed=42' \
  --tokenizer=tokenizer_v2 --tokenizer-seed=42 \
  --stop='\n\n' \
  --warmup-kv=100 \
  --batch-policy=latency
```
Notes: keep the exact same prompt set and stop seq. Do NOT let the harness substitute stop tokens. Also pin tokenizer binary hash to avoid subtle detokenization diffs.

Alex W: Requesting: run paired runs with (A) kernels=auto (B) kernels=force-cu128 (or whatever forces the older kernel) and (C) kernels=force-quant-path. Record perf counters + KV hit rates.

Jia Chen: +1. Also ensure decode params are serialized exactly — we should pass the same string to both runs (no SDK defaults). Use explicit stop bytes not logical descriptions. I'll run tokenizer_diff on the prompt set before handing over.

Omar R: If you suspect kernel choice, add env var to force kernel selection and log kernel version in the trace. Also capture batch composition histogram. Example env: KERNEL_OVERRIDE=cu128 KERNEL_LOG=1. For KV: run a warmup pass that primes the KV cache with the first 50 tokens of each session and then do the measured pass.

perf-bot: QUICK-RESULTS (from last night run) — model=redwood/gptx-8q, kernels=auto, 2m sample:
p50_latency: 32ms
p95_latency: 210ms  <-- regression vs baseline 170ms
tokens/sec: 5800
kv_hit_rate: 0.62
errors: 0.4% (mostly timeouts on long seqs)

Sophia L: Profiling snippet from a trace where p95 spiked:
```
flamegraph: hot path -> kernel_fallback_slow_attention (36%)
CPU: decode_loop -> batch_flush (12%)
GPU memcopy: repeated small copies when batch splits (14%)
KV cache: frequent misses for seq_len>128
```
Looks like for sequences around 140 tokens we fall back to a different attention kernel which increases latency. That fallback triggers when batch has heterogeneous sequence lengths.

Sophia L: I also saw that our batching heuristic lets a long request sit with several short ones, causing repeated KV writes. We should try a strict max-batch-latency policy or sequence bucketing.

Alex W: Good catch. Proposed next steps:
- Jia: run tokenizer_diff and confirm no tokenization drift.
- Omar: submit two forced-kernel runs (cu128 + quant-path) with KV warmup=200 and batch-policy=strict for 30m.
- Sophia: attach perf counters and a flamegraph export.
- I'll collect traces and do a paired latency percentile compare + kernel attribution.

Jia Chen: I'll run tokenizer_diff now and post results. If tokens differ, we abort the compare.

Omar R: I'll queue the runs on the dedicated pool; will tag runs with run_id=decode-align-1745649870 and post links. ETA: overnight.

Alex W: OK — ping when runs complete. If we still see p95 regression with kernels pinned, then we look at batching heuristics + KV behavior. Otherwise kernel selection is the culprit. Thanks :thumbsup:
